chunks: Muhammad ibn Hammam (may Allah have mercy on him) informed us, saying: Humeed ibn Ziyad narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Suma'a, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Maythami, from Za'ida ibn Qudama, from some of his men, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
When al-Qa'im rises, the people will say: How can that be, whereas his bones have been perished?
ai.seo_question: What do people say about the Imam al-Qa'im when he reappears?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Nu'mani highlights a specific eschatological sign where the public doubts the Mahdi's identity due to the perceived destruction of his physical remains, reflecting the Shia theological concept of the 'bones' (or body) being preserved or lost during the long occultation. It underscores the tension between human expectation of a visible, resurrected figure and the reality of the Imam's hidden state, a theme central to the discourse on the longevity of Imam al-Mahdi.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (13) Muhammad bin Hammam narrated from Hameed bin Ziyad from al-Hasan bin Muhammad bin Suma’a from Ahmad bin al-Hasan al-Maythami from Za’ida bin Qudama from some of his companions that Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (as) had said: “
When al-Qa’im reappears, people will say: How can that be whereas his bones have been perished?”
